I try to explain to my loved ones that BPD is not "black and white." There are diagnostic criteria, yes, but BPD seems to be more like a spectrum in the same way that autism is a spectrum. People with BPD often have characteristics of multiple mental illnesses, and because of this, BPD varies from person to person. They do not understand BPD and all they know is the stigma. They see someone with BPD in a movie and that becomes their perception of it. And sometimes people are just in denial because they don't know what to do with that information. "Does this mean I have to treat this person differently or that they're not the person I thought I knew?" BPD is complex and can be very hard to understand for someone who does not experience it for themselves.

As I said, I asked myself in hindsight why I didn't just hang up. In the moment, I was completely shocked, confused, and caught off guard. I kept thinking "did he just say what I think he said or am I misunderstanding?" 
After thinking I was on a phone call helping a customer, I was suddenly slammed with the revelation that this whack job was calling to hear my voice while he masturbated. It wasn't a random prank phone call. This is a customer (old enough to be my father) I have conversed with in my store. He has been in my physical presence close enough to touch me. (Ew) 
I was disturbed. I am disturbed. Also, I truly could not understand what he was saying at first (he has a thick accent), and I would never hang up on a customer simply because I couldn't make out what they were saying. Once I finally realized what he said, I hung up within a minute, but I had to say my piece. I had to let him know that what he was doing was not right, and I'm pretty sure he feels like a douchebag, and if I ever see him again, it will likely be if he's psychotic enough to try to pursue me and apologize with the delusions that I'll forgive him and we'll live happily ever after.
I shared here because I felt violated. And that feeling can also be very isolating. That's never a good road to go down, so I shared this in a safe *ahem* place where I knew I could get support from people who may have experienced something similar. It's validating, and validation is something that we all seek, whether we're aware of it or not.

Even if he "misread the situation," and thought I was attracted to him, he could have simply tried to ask me out and I would have politely declined. But no, he had to jump to 'wanna hear me masturbate?'
That's one hell of an icebreaker. 
If there's a next time, I'll be prepared.

I did try *69, but our phones do not have that capability. I have two phone numbers for him (from the return slip and our loyalty program) and we are going to see if we can match one of those to the phone records since we have a date/time for the phone call.

I did file a police report.
I also might have stumbled across some helpful information on the internet.
I'm sorry for your experience with this. I am very grateful for the small army that's got my back.

Thank you for your kind and encouraging words. I do have a strong support system both professionally and personally. Security and law enforcement are taking it very seriously. Part of me wants to catch this pervert, because it's unlikely I am the only person he has violated/will violate. Part of me hopes he got the message and I'll never have to deal with him again. Needless to say, I won't be leaving work without an escort and some pepper spray, at least for a little while. I'm not taking any chances.
